Q: How do I make fully customisable home page for user A:

What you're describing is called a resizable panel layout or split pane layout. The OBS-style dragging between windows is specifically called a splitter or resize handle.

If you wanted to implement something like that on your own, you might be interested in the draggable attribute and HTML Drag and Drop API:

https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Global_attributes/draggable https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTML_Drag_and_Drop_API

But if you are not into this stuff, what you are aiming to might be too much to achieve from scratch yet because it would require a very good understanding spanning across a wide knowledge of HTML/CSS/JS.

So maybe before attempting something that big, you may give a look to some existing libraries already doing the heavy lifting (for example):

  • https://gridstackjs.com/#demo
  • https://golden-layout.com/

Q: Why is this expression treated as a first member value rather than a structure value? A:

Initializer lists are used to initialize members of arrays, structures or unions.

According to the C24 Standard commpound literals are defined the following way

6.5.3.6 Compound literals

Syntax

1 compound-literal: ( storage-class-specifiersopt type-name ) braced-initializer

And according to the section 6.7.11 Initialization braced-initializer is defined the following way

6.7.11 Initialization

Syntax 1

braced-initializer:

{ }

{ initializer-list }

{ initializer-list , }

And futher:

17 Otherwise, the initializer for an object that has aggregate or union type shall be a brace-enclosed list of initializers for the elements or named members.

and

18 Each brace-enclosed initializer list has an associated current object. When no designations are present, subobjects of the current object are initialized in order according to the type of the current object: array elements in increasing subscript order, structure members in declaration order, and the first named member of a union.

So the compiler uses an object of the type struct load_con as an initializer of the first member of the new created structure of the compound literal.

Instead you could write for example

a = &(load_con){a->X, a->Y};

You may enclose in braces an initializing expression only for scalar objects like

int x = 10;
int y = { x };

For structures you may not write as for example

struct load_con b = { *a };

because the compiler will interpretate the record as an inialization with an initializer list.

You have to write

struct load_con b = *a;

Q: How to find a character at a given mouse position? A:

First off, are you using VCL or FMX? It makes a HUGE difference, as they are very different frameworks.

Assuming VCL, finding a character in a TListBox is different than finding a character in, say, a TMemo, etc. You would have to first determine which exact control is located at the mouse coordinates (such as via TWinControl.ControlAtPos() or FindDragTarget()), then determine what its underlying type is (such as via RealGetClassWindow() - see What makes RealGetWindowClass so much more real than GetClassName?), and then finally based on that type maybe ask the control to find the character within itself (if possible).

For example, for a TMemo or TRichEdit, you can simply send it an EM_CHARFROMPOS message.

But, for a TListBox, there is no such message, so it will take more work on your part (assuming the ListBox is not being custom/owner-drawn, then all bets are off). You can try using the LB_ITEMFROMPOINT and LB_GETTEXT messages to determine the item string at the coordinates, then do some some math to determine the exact character at the coordinates. Probably by using LB_GETITEMRECT to get the starting coordinate of the item string, and then using GetCharacterPlacement() to calculate the offset of each subsequent character in the item string until you reach the target coordinates.

Q: git recognizes directory as file A:

To anyone new, what worked for me was:

git reset .
git add .

I had gotten into a pickle after initializing git, then going to a parent folder and initializing git again. My first fix was to rm -rf .git but then I got into the issue where the original folder was viewed as a file.

Q: Why does a new object show [[Prototype]]: Object instead of null when expanding in Chrome console? A:

Object literal syntax creates an object that inherits from Object. To create an object with a null prototype do

const obj = Object.create(null);
console.dir(obj);

or use a literal that overrides the default __proto__ property:

const obj2 = { __proto__: null };
console.dir(obj2);
